root_idea.summary: The root centers on an edge, extremity, or boundary, and on movement of the eyelids in looking.
root_idea.development: The edge sense extends to sides, portions, and the ends of periods; eyelid movement gives rise to the meanings eye, glance, and gaze. Related developments include selecting or acquiring something new, as though taking from an outer or newly reached portion.

senses.definition: An extremity, end, side, region, or portion of something.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of material things and of periods of time: أَطْرَافُ النَّهَارِ and طَرَفَا النَّهَارِ refer to the ends or portions of the day, while أَطْرَافُ الأَرْضِ refers to its borders, sides, or districts. In the Quranic expression about reducing the land from its edges, the phrase has also been interpreted figuratively as reducing its inhabitants, produce, or learned and notable people.

senses.definition: A look, glance, or gaze; the act of looking.
senses.usage_conditions: The word can denote the movement of the eyelids in looking and, by association, the resulting glance or gaze. It includes a look that returns or is withdrawn and a restrained or lowered gaze.

senses.definition: The eye or eyes, viewed as the organ or faculty of sight.
senses.usage_conditions: The eye sense is a substantive development from the eyelid movement associated with looking; in Quranic usage the plural or collective sense can refer to eyes or their gaze.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To blink or move the eyelids while looking; to look at, see, or direct one's sight toward something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes the verb used of the eye itself and of directing the sight with the eye.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike, hurt, or injure someone's eye so that it sheds tears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be the eye itself; the cause can be a garment, object, grief, or weeping.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slap or blow delivered to the extremity of the eye, and by extension a striking upon the head.
To turn or draw the sight away or back from something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially with the sight as object or with a command to turn the gaze away.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To withhold someone from another person or place by diverting or occupying him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A business or occupation may be the cause of the withholding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To drive someone away.
A blinking eye as a metonym for a living being; in the negative, the absence of a blinking eye means that none remain alive or that they have been slain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic and figurative use based on the visible blinking of a living eye.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, to graze the sides or outer portions of pasture, moving from one pasture to another rather than remaining with one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also applied to a she-camel that samples pastures successively.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be newly or recently acquired; to be new, fresh, or good in its freshness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a verbal description of recent acquisition or freshness, distinct from the derived noun for a newly acquired thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Remote or extended in descent from an ancestor; in some descriptions, possessing a long line of ancestors.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical tradition records contrasting applications concerning old descent and recently established nobility.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To attack or fight around the flank or outer part of an army and drive those on the side back toward the main body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of driving back the foremost or rearward members of a group upon the rest.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dye or color the ends of the fingers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The extremities of the fingers are the part treated.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make an extremity pointed, tapering, or slender.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of making a horse's ear pointed; figuratively, meanings or expressions may be made pointed or embellished.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To choose or select a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The choice is understood through the notion of taking what is at an outer or selected point.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, to lose a tooth or teeth through extreme age.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the effects of advanced age on the teeth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To close the eyelids.
To make ornamental, colored, or figured borders at the ends or sides of a garment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction concerns the two ends or sides of the garment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give someone a novel, rare, or pleasing thing, especially something newly acquired or not previously given to that person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be a gift, property, or other valued novelty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bring or tell someone new information or tidings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The newness of the report is part of the conventional construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause those around someone to wonder through something novel or strange.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may also mean that the surrounding people acquired a novel piece of information through it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Numerous or distinguished ancestors, especially ancestors of note.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The meaning concerns ancestry and inherited distinction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a country or land, to abound in the pasture called طَرِيفَة.
To become pointed, tapering, or slender at the extremity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form can describe a thing acquiring an extremity or pointed end.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become or be at an extremity or side; to take the side of a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The latter use is expressed by taking from or taking the side of something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go far aside from urine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression concerning the direction or placement of urination.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the sun, to approach setting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A temporal extension of approaching an extremity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a sudden or unexpected attack upon a people's territory or dwellings.
To take something from its side or take its side portion.
To purchase a thing new.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form denotes acquiring something as a new purchase.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To count, esteem, or regard something as new.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of discourse that a listener regards as novel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To find, gain, or acquire something newly.
Of a woman, to choose new men rather than remain with one husband.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use modeled on the camel that samples one pasture after another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of camels, to choose or select pasture, especially to take its first or freshest part.
A named star or pair of stars associated with the face of Leo and a lunar mansion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Astronomical nomenclature; the exact stellar identification varies in the cited descriptions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The fingers or fingertips.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural can function in the sense of a singular fingertip in some expressions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A variety of long, slender grapes likened to the fingers of maidens.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional name for a grape variety.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind of black serpent said to strike with both its nose and its tail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A zoological or folkloric designation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The extremities of an animal or body, including its fore and hind parts, limbs, hands or feet, and head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The exact members included vary by expression and authority.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an idiom about a sick person, one of the two terminal outcomes: recovery or death.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The two outcomes are conceived as the two ends of the illness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In idioms, the two bodily ends, especially the mouth and anus; related expressions may use the two ends for the tongue and sexual organ, or for the upper and lower halves of the body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are fixed figurative expressions, not a general anatomical definition of every occurrence of طَرَف.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Noble or generous on both sides of one's parentage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The two sides are the paternal and maternal lines; some related expressions extend the phrase to the father's and mother's lineage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person's close kin, including parents, siblings, paternal uncles, and relations whom one may not marry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative plural use based on the person's familial sides.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The lower orders of the people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited lexical note regards this usage as probably post-classical.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Beside, aside, or apart; in related usage, on the part of someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are prepositional and idiomatic constructions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An affair has two possible ways or alternatives, either of which may be chosen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The alternatives are conceived as two ends or sides of the affair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Choice or selected subjects of discourse; in some usage, friendly colloquies with indirect expressions and allusions.
Flesh or meat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A choice, generous, or handsome horse, especially one admired for its beauty, breeding, or form.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word can describe a recently acquired horse and a horse with notably long legs or neck and pointed ears.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A generous or noble young man or man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective may concern general generosity or noble ancestry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Recent or newly established nobility of lineage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized and sometimes contrasting lineage use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman whose discourse is good and esteemed as novel by those who hear it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed descriptive expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One desirous of possessing everything that one sees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use describing acquisitive desire.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Produce of the earth still enclosed in its calyxes.
A wink or twinkling of the eye, namely the closing or movement of an eyelid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used in comparisons for extreme speed or a very brief interval.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A red spot of blood in the eye caused by a blow or another cause.
A brand or hot-iron mark consisting only of a line and lacking lateral portions.
An injury or hurt of the eye that causes it to shed tears.
A newly acquired, rare, strange, or pleasing thing, especially a welcome or novel gift.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural refers to such rare and pleasing gifts or novelties.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single tree of the species called طَرْفَاء.
Remoteness in lineage from the chief or oldest ancestor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It is contrasted with قُعْدَى, which denotes nearer descent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tamarisk-like tree or collective kind of tree, including the plant commonly identified as tamarisk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical accounts differ over whether the word is singular, plural, or a collective noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where طَرَفَة trees grow.
The portion cut from the extremities of corn or other seed-produce.
A desert tent made of skin or leather.
Property newly acquired, as opposed to inherited property; also a thing that is new, fresh, strange, rare, varied in color, or pleasing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use of طَرِيفٌ and related forms for something recently acquired or newly presented, contrasted with تَلِيدٌ, تَالِدٌ, or تِلَادٌ; the associated descriptions of strangeness, freshness, variety, and pleasing novelty are included in this branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mature, white and dry, or otherwise choice kind of herbage and pasture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word can refer to specified grasses or to the first and best pasture selected by cattle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Anything new, recent, fresh, or choice; by extension, a choice article or subject.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This nominal use is distinct from the specialized pasture plant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The side portions of a tent raised to permit looking out; in another account, rings and cords attached to its skirts.
A large quantity of property or cattle, conceived as something that overwhelms or dazzles the eye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic, figurative expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Things newly originated by later inventive or creative faculties.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression is used of novel intellectual productions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Beasts of prey that seize or carry off the animals they hunt.
In a poetic description, two verses that are strange or excellent, ornamented at their two extremities, or beautified in their first and last feet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The transmitted wording and interpretation vary.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A square garment or cloak of fine cloth, especially khazz, with ornamental, colored, or figured borders.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The borders may be at the two ends or sides.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Clouds, by comparison with bordered garments.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative plural use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An animal marked with contrasting color at its extremities, such as a horse white at the head and tail or a sheep colored at the ends of its tail or ears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The exact color pattern varies by animal and account.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a horse, repeatedly improved in generosity through descent from generous sires and dams.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This interpretation belongs to a disputed poetic reading.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man or horse that fights around the flank or outer part of an army or hostile company and repels those on the side.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related form and the transmitted poetic reading vary.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Looked at exclusively of others; the person or thing singled out for someone's gaze.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial use of the looking verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An eye whose lids move in looking, or an eye struck or hurt so that it sheds tears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The context determines whether the blinking or injured-eye sense is intended.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman described as having a languishing or wandering gaze, or as looking at men rather than remaining devoted to one husband.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The authorities preserve several explanations, including a metaphor of an injured or languid eye.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land abounding in the herbage called طَرِيفَة.
A newly purchased camel, especially one bought from another part of the country and still longing for its accustomed place.
A man who does not remain constant in an affair or companionship.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The transmitted text may intend a woman or wife rather than a general affair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The first or beginning part of the days.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed temporal expression.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Eyelid is stated within the Quran-attested eye/gaze branch.
Synonymic pointer without additional lexical content.
Quranic interpretation remains within the edge/side sense.
Contrasting recent-nobility usage is stated in the target.
Fresh, strange, and pleasing are subdescriptions of the new-property branch.

cautions: The Quranic occurrences of طَرْف and طَرَف represent overlapping eye/gaze and edge/portion branches; translations such as “eye,” “gaze,” “glance,” “ends,” and “borders” reflect construction and context.
The interpretation of أَطْرَافِ الأَرْضِ in the Quran varies between physical borders or districts and figurative reduction of inhabitants, produce, or learned people.
Several Classical Arabic entries preserve variant authorities or disputed readings, especially lineage adjectives, poetic descriptions, and the idiomatic uses of مَطْرُوفَة.
